title: SPI-RDT assessment template
description: The full instrument: Part A context fields, the five scored sections, and the scoring rules. Stored as the JSON document in templates.definition. Immutable once published — editing copy-on-writes to a new version.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema, not of the template. Lets a reader tell a structural change from a content change.

code.description: Instrument identifier. 'spi-rdt' for the canonical instrument; forks keep it so scores stay comparable.

version.description: Semver. Publishing freezes it; edits produce a new version.

locales.description: Locales this template carries text for. Every localised string must have a key for default_locale at minimum.

source.description: Provenance of the content, so a generated template can be traced back and regenerated.

context_fields.description: Part A. Characterises the facility and testing site. NOT scored.

localised.description: Text keyed by locale. Never a bare string — translations are a launch requirement, and a bare string here is what makes them a retrofit.

responses.description: Point value per response. NA is excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator — it is not a zero.

round_dp.description: Decimal places the percentage is rounded to BEFORE banding. Rounding first means 89.995 becomes 90.00 and lands in the top band; banding on the unrounded value would not, and the boundaries are where certification disputes happen.

bands.description: Certification levels, ascending by min_percent. Each band runs up to the next band's min_percent; the last is open-ended. Expressed as a lower bound only so bands cannot overlap or leave gaps. Localised per the User's Guide, which states countries adjust these during tool customisation.

points.description: Null only for an excluded response.

excluded.description: When true this response is removed from the possible total rather than scored zero.

scope.description: 'assessment' answers once per assessment. 'pathogen' repeats for every pathogen assessed — this is what makes Section 4 work, and why the possible total scales with pathogen count.

optional.description: When true the whole section can be marked not applicable, contributing nothing to score or possible total. Section 5 where a site refers no specimens.

applicability_field.description: Assessment field deciding whether an optional section applies, e.g. refers_specimens. One question instead of nine N/A answers.

code.description: Stable identifier such as 1.1 or 4.23. This is the join key for exports, reporting and the question catalog — never row position, which silently misaligns once templates are customised.

guidance.description: How to assess it: what to look for, what evidence counts. From the User's Guide.

criteria.description: What each response means for THIS question. Shown inline while answering — the single cheapest way to get consistent scoring between assessors, and something the paper form cannot do.

na_allowed.description: Whether Not Applicable may be selected. Deliberately per-question data rather than code: the Checklist prints an N/A box on every row while the User's Guide defines a condition for only six, and allowing N/A everywhere inflates percentages and undermines the certification banding.

comment_required_for.description: Responses that oblige a comment. The checklist requires describing the gap for P and N, and stating why the question does not apply for NA.

options.description: For select_one. Stored by key, so labels can be localised or relabelled without rewriting stored answers.

specify.description: Whether choosing this option opens a free-text box — the checklist's 'Other (Specify):' pattern.

fields.description: For repeat: the per-row fields, e.g. the Part A staff roster of name and title.
